audit.why: 53.84% over 704 games supports FAV / 6-10 against an 8/10 carry threat.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four level rows disagreed with the packet chart and with their own prose: Level 1, Levels 4-5 and Level 6 all said Skill while the packet gives Olaf and the whys describe Olaf winning outright; 2+ items said Olaf while the packet says Swain and whys[6] says he reclaims it.
audit.why: The chart read 'contested' precisely through Olaf's dominant stretch and 'safe' at the point Swain takes over.
audit.corrected: phases[0]/[3]/[4]/[6].side and win[0]/[3]/[4]/[6] flipped in matched pairs, ratings moved to follow, all four phase whys rewritten around Nevermove and Demonic Ascension.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page named no Swain ability (packet defect), attributed Soul Fragments to his ultimate ('R soul-drain', 'R soul fragments', 'R soul-stacks'), called Vision of Empire a 'W-bomb' with sustain attached, claimed Ragnarok 'cleanses'/'strips' his CC, and credited Ragnarok with move speed.
audit.why: Soul Fragments come from Ravenous Flock, the passive, and Vision of Empire grants one when it hits a champion — the ultimate drains, it does not collect fragments. Ragnarok's Riot text is passive armour and magic resist plus immunity to disables while attacking; there is no move speed in it. The decisive unstated interaction is Nevermove itself: the outgoing wave does nothing, and it is the RETURN pass that roots — so the dodge is on the way back, which is the opposite of how players instinctively sidestep it.
audit.corrected: Named Ravenous Flock, Death's Hand, Vision of Empire, Nevermove (850 range, 12s) and Demonic Ascension (120s); moved Soul Fragments to the passive and W; stated the return-pass root; replaced every cleanse claim and dropped the invented move speed.

audit.why: Unlike most of this champion's pages, the anti-heal advice here is genuinely right — Ravenous Flock heals and Demonic Ascension drains, so Executioner's Calling has a real target.
audit.corrected: Left the itemization line alone; only spikes[2] was rewritten to say what the anti-heal is actually for.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1] ('Build MR') and dosFull[2] ('R to cleanse his E root') both carried unrelated bodies.
audit.why: Neither told the reader how to do the thing in its heading.
audit.corrected: Bodies rewritten to match their headings.

edits.before: Swain has no real answer to your level 1-3 pressure — he is a slow, immobile drain-mage with no dash. Open with Q to land the slow, walk in, and weave E's true damage; his Q-poke and W-bomb simply cannot match a guaranteed Reckless Swing chunk. The one thing to respect is his E: if he lands the bolt it pulls and roots you, so trade after he whiffs it or bait it with a feint before you commit your axe.
edits.after: Swain has no answer to your level 1-3 pressure — a slow, immobile drain-mage with no dash. Open with Q to land the slow, walk in, and weave E's true damage; Death's Hand and Vision of Empire cannot match a guaranteed Reckless Swing chunk. The one thing to respect is Nevermove: the outgoing wave does nothing, the RETURN pass is what roots you, so watch it come back and sidestep that, not the throw.

edits.before: This is your takeover. Through 4-5 your axe-reset slows and W-omnivamp let you sit on him in every short trade, and his pre-6 kit can't peel you off. At 6 Ragnarok is the lane-winner — it strips his E-root and W-slow off you and gives armor/MR plus move speed straight at him, so you ult into his peel and run him down or tower-dive him. Just don't ult into nothing; save it for when he commits E.
edits.after: This is your takeover. Through 4-5 your axe resets and Tough It Out's shield let you sit on him in every short trade, and his pre-6 kit cannot peel you off. At 6 Ragnarok is the lane-winner — while you keep swinging you are immune to Nevermove's root, and its passive armour and MR blunt his magic damage, so you ult into his peel and run him down or tower-dive. Don't ult into nothing; save it for when he commits Nevermove.

edits.before: You have to close this before it goes long. Once Swain reaches 2+ items his R becomes a sustained AOE soul-drain that heals him faster than your W can out-trade, and in teamfights he pulls and roots your carries from max range while you tunnel one target. Your flat E true damage and short-fight kit lose value here — so convert every early lead into towers, dives, and objectives and never let this become a 30-minute scaling fight.
edits.after: You have to close this before it goes long. Once Swain reaches 2+ items Demonic Ascension is a sustained drain off every nearby champion, minion and monster, healing him faster than you can trade, and Nevermove roots your carries from 850 and pulls them in while you tunnel one target. Your flat E true damage and short-fight kit lose value here — so convert every early lead into towers, dives and objectives and never let this become a 30-minute scaling fight.
